content.p: Mehul Choksi is a diamond businessman from India who has been named as one of the prime accused in a large bank fraud case. He has not been convicted of any offence in the reports reviewed here. The allegations concern letters of undertaking that the CBI says were issued to his companies without a sanctioned limit or cash margin. Since 2018 he has been outside India: in Antigua and Barbuda, and for a time in Belgium, where he lived on a residency card. His case has moved through courts in the Caribbean and in Belgium.

The case came to light in February 2018, when the bank told the stock exchange that it had detected "fraudulent and unauthorised transactions" worth Rs 11,380 crore at a branch in South Mumbai, according to Scroll. The branch was the Brady House branch. Investigators allege that officials of the bank issued letters of undertaking, a form of guarantee a bank gives on behalf of a client to a foreign lender, to companies linked to Choksi and his nephew Nirav Modi. Under such a guarantee, the guarantor bank carries the liability if the client does not repay the foreign lender. The CBI alleges that this is what happened here, leaving PNB exposed.

The CBI's supplementary chargesheet, reported by Outlook in June 2021, said the probe had found 165 letters of undertaking and 58 foreign letters of credit issued to Choksi's companies. It alleged that the officials acted from 2011 to 2017 in conspiracy with Choksi and company executives, and that the letters were issued without a sanctioned limit or cash margin and without entries in the bank's central banking system. The same report said the agency had charged the accused with criminal conspiracy, cheating, breach of trust, disappearance of evidence and criminal misconduct by a public servant. The CBI said its probe was continuing.

Choksi left India in early January 2018. Scroll reported that he fled a few weeks before the fraud was made public. The News Minute reported that he had taken Antiguan citizenship that year and later deposited his cancelled Indian passport and a fee with the Indian High Commission in Guyana, which is also accredited to Antigua and Barbuda. Its sources said the Indian government would keep pursuing him through diplomatic and legal channels.

The size of the loss is reported in several ways, and the figures should not be combined. Scroll and Organiser put the loss to PNB at about Rs 6,097 crore. The CBI, as reported by Outlook, said Choksi's companies were accused of siphoning off Rs 7,080 crore through these instruments, and that Modi's companies had allegedly cheated for over Rs 6,498 crore. Outlook also put the alleged total at over Rs 13,000 crore. The News Minute and Organiser each used larger totals, Rs 13,500 crore and Rs 13,850 crore. The Wire, reporting the Belgian order, described a chargesheet for a Rs 6,400 crore bank fraud within a wider Rs 13,000 crore case. The reports reviewed do not show a trial verdict on any of these figures.

Choksi lived in Antigua and Barbuda for several years, and he was a citizen there. In 2021 his claim that he had been abducted from Antigua became a question for the government there. Antigua's Prime Minister Gaston Browne told parliament that he was not aware of any conclusive proof that Choksi had been abducted and taken to Dominica, although, as Scroll reported him saying, there was information in the public domain that he had been. Browne also said that law enforcement in Antigua might have been looking into people of interest. According to Scroll, Choksi filed a five-page complaint with Antigua police on June 2, 2021, in which he said a woman he knew helped his abductor and that he had been taken to Dominica to be interviewed by an Indian politician. The reports reviewed do not say whether that complaint produced charges.

Choksi was detained in Dominica in late May 2021. The dates differ. Scroll reported that he was caught on the night of May 26, after he had allegedly fled Antigua, and that he was reportedly trying to escape to Cuba. Outlook and ETV Bharat gave May 23 as the arrest date, and Outlook's report on the supplementary chargesheet gave May 24. All the accounts say he was charged with illegal entry. Outlook and ETV Bharat add that he was declared a prohibited immigrant.

On June 12, 2021, the Dominica High Court refused him bail, calling him "a flight risk", according to Scroll. He was held in judicial custody after that. In July 2021 he asked the High Court in Roseau to quash the criminal proceedings against him. Outlook and ETV Bharat, citing a Caribbean outlet, reported that the application named the immigration minister, the acting police chief in Roseau and the investigating officer, and argued that the charge was "not a product of their independent judgement" but was "dictated" by representatives of the Indian government. In that filing, Choksi said he had told Dominican police about being kidnapped from Antigua, and that they had not investigated. The reports reviewed do not show how the High Court ruled on that application.
content.h2: Arrest in Belgium and the extradition courts
content.p: Choksi was arrested in Belgium in April 2025. The Belgian federal public service of justice confirmed to Organiser and others that he was arrested on Saturday, April 12, 2025, and was being held in anticipation of further judicial proceedings, and that India had submitted an extradition request. The Wire gave April 11 as the date of his provisional arrest. Choksi's lawyer, Vijay Aggarwal, said the defence would argue on two grounds: that the case was political, and that there were concerns about proper treatment for his health condition in India. Organiser reported that Aggarwal also said Choksi had not been declared a fugitive because he had cooperated with Indian agencies.

The Antwerp Court of Appeal ruled in October 2025 against him. Scroll reported that the court called his arguments against extradition "irrelevant" and found that he had not produced sufficient evidence of a risk of a flagrant denial of justice or of inhuman or degrading treatment in India. The Wire quoted the order as saying that the offences could not be considered political and that it could not be inferred from the documents that he had been kidnapped in Antigua on Indian instructions. The order also recorded Indian authorities' statement that, if extradited, he would be held in Arthur Road Prison in Mumbai.

In December 2025 the Court of Cassation, Belgium's highest court, rejected his appeal. Its advocate general, Henri Vanderlinden, told Hindustan Times, as Scroll reported, that the ruling meant the Antwerp decision stood. The reports reviewed do not confirm that Choksi has been handed over to India.

Several points are still disputed or unresolved in the reports reviewed. His lawyers have described the case as political, and Choksi's account of abduction has not been tested in any court that the reports reviewed describe. The Belgian court said the offences could not be considered political and that the documents did not show he had been kidnapped on Indian instructions; it called its order a first step towards extradition. The amount lost, the dates of the Dominica detention and the outcome of the Dominica application all depend on which report is followed. Whether the case before the special court in Mumbai will reach a verdict, and when, is not settled by any source reviewed.
